What are the three primary anthropogenic nutrient sources on Tutuila identified in the section?
records.ground_truth_answer: On-Site wastewater Disposal Systems (OSDS); widespread small-scale pig farming operations; and agricultural fertilizers.
ground_truth_chunks: The three primary anthropogenic nutrient 187 sources on Tutuila have been previously determined to be: (1) On-Site wastewater Disposal 188 Systems (OSDS), (2) widespread small-scale pig farming operations, and (3) agricultural 189 fertilizers (Falkland et al., 2002; Polidoro et al., 2017; Shuler et al., 2017); but the relative 190 impact of each source on coastal ecosystems remains poorly understood.

records.question: How many 222Rn measurements were taken in the time-series at the fixed nearshore location, and over what duration?
ground_truth_chunks:
We assessed temporal (tide-

dependent) variability with a time-series of 261 <sup>222</sup>Rn measurements taken from a fixed nearshore 262 location over a 48-hour period.

Dissolved <sup>222</sup>Rn was used as a groundwater tracer in a temporally and spatially distributed non-steady-state radon flux model to calculate bay-wide SGD rates following the methods of Burnett & Dulaiova (2003) and Dulaiova et al. (2010).

records.section_heading: 305 3.2.3 SGD Flux Scaling, Fresh and Recirculated Fractions
records.question: What ambient 222Rn activity value was used in the SGD flux model for oceanic or atmospheric sources?
records.ground_truth_answer: An ambient 222Rn activity of 0.03 dpm/L was used.
ground_truth_chunks: We assumed that ambient 309 <sup>222</sup>Rn activities from oceanic or atmospheric sources were comparable to those found in the Hawaiian Islands, and used an ambient 310 <sup>222</sup>Rn activity of 0.03 dpm/L (Kelly and Glenn, 2012), a local excess 311 <sup>222</sup>Rn activity of 0.08 dpm/L supported by in situ <sup>226</sup>Ra (Street et al., 2008), and an offshore 312 <sup>222</sup>Rn activity of 0.087 dpm/L, derived from the offshore <sup>226</sup> 313 Ra (Fröllje et al., 2016).

records.question: What were the top three most sensitive nutrient parameters identified during the SWAT nutrient transport calibration?
records.ground_truth_answer: (1) the filtration capacity of stream edge; (2) the denitrification threshold soil water content; and (3) the in‑stream rate constant for hydrolysis of organic N to NH4+.
ground_truth_chunks: The nutrient transport calibration used the same methods as the hydrologic portion of SWAT, with the top three most sensitive nutrient parameters being: (1) the filtration capacity of stream edge, (2) the denitrification threshold soil water content, and (3) the in-stream rate constant for hydrolysis of organic N to  $NH_4^+$ .

Model calibration attempts were suspended with the best simulation only able to bracket 60% of the calibration data (nine of the NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> measurements and fifteen of the NO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup> measurements) at the 95% PPU.

records.question: What arithmetic mean fractions of high-level baseflow and recently discharged basal-lens baseflow at site S1 were used for nutrient flux calculations?
records.ground_truth_answer: The arithmetic mean fractions used were 67% high-level baseflow and 33% recently discharged basal-lens baseflow.
ground_truth_chunks: Results from 2014 data indicate stream water at site S1 was composed of 67% high-level baseflow (2,368 m<sup>3</sup>/d) and 33% (1,156 m<sup>3</sup>/d) recently discharged basal-lens baseflow, and <sup>222</sup>Rn-based unmixing results from 2016 data show that stream water at site S1 was composed of 66% high-level baseflow (2,412 m<sup>3</sup>/d) and 34% (1,217 m<sup>3</sup>/d) recently discharged basal-lens baseflow.

When these four separate and independent assessments of streamflow partitioning are averaged, the arithmetic mean fractions of high-level baseflow and recently discharged basal-lens baseflow at site S1 are 67% and 33%, respectively, which were the fractions we used for calculations of nutrient fluxes through these pathways.

records.section_heading: 571 4.3.3 Total SGD and Nutrient Flux Scaling with Coastal Survey Data
records.question: What were the calculated scaling factors for the southern and northern plumes relative to the central plume?
records.ground_truth_answer: 0.10 ± 0.08 for the southern plume and 0.32 ± 0.21 for the northern plume.
ground_truth_chunks: Calculated 577 scaling factors were 0.10 ± 0.08 for the southern plume and 0.32 ± 0.21 for the northern 578 plume, or in other words, SGD rates estimated during the survey showed the southern and 579 northern plumes discharged 10% and 32%, respectively, of the central plume's SGD rate (see 580 section 4.3.2).

records.question: What does the correlation between δ15N_N+N values and DIN values suggest about the source of sampled DIN?
records.ground_truth_answer: It suggests a large component of sampled DIN originates from a high δ15N_N+N source, such as wastewater or manure, rather than synthetic agricultural fertilizers.
ground_truth_chunks: 742 While extensive source dependent nutrient tracing efforts were not performed in this study, moderate correlation between elevated DIN concentrations and δ 743 <sup>15</sup>NN+N isotopes in baseflow and coastal surface water (r<sup>2</sup> 744 of 0.93 and 0.45, respectively) provided insight into the transport history of nutrients from source to sink.

The correlation between δ 745 <sup>15</sup>NN+N values and DIN values suggests a large component of sampled DIN originates from a high δ 746 <sup>15</sup>NN+N source, 747 such as wastewater or manure, as opposed to synthetic agricultural fertilizers, which typically

have δ 748 <sup>15</sup>NN+N values near 0 ‰ (Kendall and Aravena, 2000).
